correctness.rationale: For any continuous h:T²→T with winding vector v=(m,n), and any F homotopic to T_A, the integral cohomology rows of D=(h,h∘F) are v,vA, so deg D=det(v;vA)=b m²+(d-a)mn−c n². A continuous injective map of compact T² into T² is onto by invariance of domain, hence a homeomorphism and degree ±1. Conversely if Q_A(v)=±1, U with rows v,vA is unimodular and linear character h_v gives D=Ux, a torus automorphism; Cayley–Hamilton yields UA=[[0,1],[-det A,tr A]]U. For F sufficiently C1-close to T_A, same character gives a local diffeomorphism covering of degree ±1, hence globally one-sheeted. Examples A0=[[3,2],[-3,4]] and B0=[[0,1],[-18,7]] share trace 7, determinant 18 and eigenvalues conjugate with modulus sqrt(18)>1, hence identical all-n periodic counts, entropy log18 and uniform one-sided Bernoulli isomorphism by expanding torus theorem. B has character x1 yielding identity two-delay, while Q_A0=2m²+mn+3n²=((4m+n)²+23n²)/8 has minimum positive 2 and never ±1, so no continuous two-delay injection for A0 or homotopic F. The sensor x1 has degree 2 and exactly two sheets. Independent exact SymPy checked trace/determinant and first 24 fixed counts, Q square completion and finite grid |m|,|n|<=40; the square-completion and topology, not finite grid, establish all integers/sensors.
